The old way vs. the new way

Running a dental group shouldn't mean guessing where the revenue went.

THE OLD WAY

Revenue leaks quietly, all month long.

  • Cancellations get noticed only when the chair is already empty.
  • Treatment plans go cold in a chart until someone happens to look.
  • Every location runs its own report, in its own PMS, on its own schedule.
  • By month-end, nobody remembers why a number moved.
THE NEW WAY

One queue, updated the moment something changes.

  • A gap opens and ChairCommand values it, then finds who's most likely to fill it.
  • AI drafts the outreach; your team reviews and approves before anything sends.
  • Every location rolls up to the same scorecard, whatever PMS it runs.
  • Every recovered dollar is logged — date, outcome, owner.
AI workflows

Meet ChairCommand's AI copilots.

Every recommendation shows its reason, its source records and a confidence score — and nothing goes out to a patient or a payer until your staff approves it.

DAILY COORDINATION

Four actions, prioritized before your day starts.

Each morning, the AI Morning Manager reviews appointments, confirmations and eligibility exceptions, then drafts who should do what — assign front desk to confirmations, route eligibility checks, hand the highest-value plan to the treatment coordinator.

Confidence 96% on today's brief
AI Morning Manager
CAPACITY RECOVERY

A gap and a match, found in the same moment.

The moment a 90-minute opening appears, the Schedule Recovery Copilot matches it against unscheduled treatment plans by duration, location and patient preference — then drafts the message asking if they'd like to move up.

Before a claim goes out, the Insurance Copilot checks it against the procedure record, attachment checklist and payer pattern — and drafts the missing clinical narrative so nothing gets denied for a paperwork gap.

Product

Turn practice-management data into daily action.

Your PMS was built to run the appointment book and the chart. It wasn't built to tell you what's slipping through the cracks. ChairCommand is the layer that does — screenshots below are the real product, from the public sales demo.

01 — AI workflows

AI prepares the work. Your team stays in control.

Every recommendation shows its reason, its source records, a confidence score, and an approval step — nothing goes out to a patient or a payer until your staff signs off. It's automation you can audit, not a black box.

  • Detect → explain → draft → staff approves → record outcome
  • An AI Morning Manager, Schedule Recovery Copilot and Insurance Copilot working the queue
  • Confidence score and "why it surfaced" on every draft
AI Workflows
02 — Prioritized work queue

One ranked list of what actually matters today.

Unscheduled treatment, denied claims, aging claims and unpaid balances all land in a single queue, ranked by dollar value and urgency — not buried across three different PMS reports nobody has time to pull.

  • Every item shows its dollar value and how it was found
  • Assign an owner and mark it open or resolved
  • A daily AI brief summarizes what changed since yesterday
Work Queue
03 — Schedule gap recovery

Know a gap is opening before the chair sits empty.

Cancellations and no-shows account for roughly a fifth of scheduled chair time industry-wide. ChairCommand matches every open chair hour to the specific patients most likely to fill it, ranked by fit and value, with outreach ready to go.

  • Open chair hours valued in real dollars, not just a blank slot
  • Best patients to contact, ranked by fit and value
  • One-click outreach per recommendation
Schedule Gaps
04 — Treatment & financing

Diagnosed treatment doesn't go cold in a chart.

Every case is tracked from presentation through insurance estimate, financing option and e-signature to scheduled care — with a case-status field and a dollar value attached at every stage, so nothing valuable just sits.

  • Phased treatment plans with estimated insurance and patient portion
  • Illustrative monthly financing option shown alongside the case
  • Request e-signature straight from the case
Treatment Plans
05 — One patient chart

Registration, insurance and history in one place, across locations.

Household relationships, verified insurance coverage, signed forms and medical alerts follow the patient wherever they're seen — so a patient who visits two locations in your group doesn't look like two different people.

  • Household relationships linked across visits
  • Verified insurance coverage on the chart
  • Medical alerts surfaced before treatment
Patients
06 — For groups & DSOs

One scorecard, every location, the same numbers.

Solo practices are only part of the market — a growing share of production now runs through multi-location groups. ChairCommand rolls every office up against the same production and collections goals, with a recommended action for each.

  • Production and collections tracked against goal, per location
  • "On pace" vs. "needs intervention" called out automatically
  • A recommended next move for every location, not just a number

Why ChairCommand

Practices aren't losing patients. They're losing visibility.

Every practice-management system already holds the answer to where production is leaking — it's in the cancellation log, the treatment-plan table, the recall list. What's missing isn't the data. It's the time to turn it into a report, every single day, on top of running a practice.

ChairCommand exists to close that gap. It's not a new system for your team to learn or a rip-and-replace of the PMS you already trust — it's a thin, read-only layer that watches the data you're already generating and turns it into a short list of things worth acting on today, with AI doing the drafting and your team doing the approving.

The goal isn't a prettier report at the end of the month. It's catching a cancellation before the chair sits empty, a treatment plan before it goes cold, and a claim before it ages past the point anyone remembers to chase it.

In practice

One brief instead of three reports.

Every morning

Leadership gets one number, not three dashboards.

The AI Brief reads like a short memo from a chief of staff: what's newly at risk, what changed since yesterday, and which location needs a call today — not a spreadsheet someone has to interpret.

AI Brief
Across a group

Every location held to the same daily checklist.

Each office gets its own operating score, its own gap to goal, and a short, specific checklist — fill this opening, resolve this claim — so "how's that location doing" has an actual answer instead of a guess.

Locations
Who it's for

Built for practices that have outgrown guessing.

Independent & growing practices

Solo and small-group practices still make up the majority of the market, and the ones investing in an operating layer like ChairCommand are the ones competing hardest with larger groups on efficiency, not just chair count.

Multi-location groups & DSOs

Once a group crosses two or three locations, "ask the office manager" stops working as a reporting strategy. ChairCommand gives ownership and regional managers one consistent scorecard across every office.

Trust & access

A layer on top of your data — not a new place for it to live.

ChairCommand is built to sit alongside clinical software, not to become another system that holds sensitive patient records.

Read-only by default

ChairCommand reads scheduling, production and treatment data from your PMS. It doesn't write back to the chart or touch clinical records.

API-based, not a rip-and-replace

Connection happens through your existing PMS's API. There's no migration, and your team keeps working in the system they already know.
